claims.text: NiTi shape memory alloys exhibit temperature-dependent changes in plastic deformation behavior across the martensitic transformation region.
Martensitic NiTi has a softer and more plastic response than austenitic NiTi.
Austenitic NiTi has a stiffer response than martensitic NiTi.
NiTi is in the austenitic phase at elevated temperatures.
The relevant martensitic transformation range may span approximately 40–60 °C, depending on the NiTi alloy.
Temperature-controlled loading across the transformation range induces a martensitic-to-austenitic change in NiTi's microstructural configuration.
The martensitic-to-austenitic transformation alters dislocation mobility in NiTi.
The martensitic-to-austenitic transformation alters the active slip systems in NiTi.
Changes in dislocation mobility and active slip systems modify NiTi's yield strength and plastic deformation behavior.
Below the transformation temperature, martensitic NiTi has lower yield strength and higher plastic strain than austenitic NiTi.
Above the transformation temperature, austenitic NiTi has higher yield strength and reduced plasticity.
Significant temperature-dependent differences in plastic deformation are confined to the phase-transformation window, with minimal changes outside it.
The quantitative changes in yield strength and plastic strain depend on alloy composition, processing history, and experimental conditions.
